message.content:
Sure! Here’s an easy way to grab the current date‑time directly from PowerShell (the built‑in shell on modern Windows):

```cmd
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ^
    "$now=(Get-Date); Write-Host $now.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH\\:mm\\:ss')"
```

When you paste this into Command Prompt (`cmd.exe`) and hit **Enter**, it will print something like:

```
2026-05-18 14:32:07
```

That format shows:
* Year–month–day  
* Hours (24‑hour clock), minutes, seconds  

If you prefer UTC instead of your local timezone, replace `(Get-Date)` with `(Get-Date -UFormat %s)` or simply add `.UtcNow`:

```cmd
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ^
    "$(Get-Date -AsUTC).ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ')"
```

This prints the same timestamp but marked as Coordinated Universal Time (e.g., `2026-05-18T19:32:07Z`).
